artworks.title: Pasquariello Truonno and Meo Squaquara
artworks.description: This is a print of two people wearing elaborate costumes in an open space. The people appear to be adorned in theatrical attire, including masks that give them exaggerated facial features such as long noses and deep-set eyes.  The two people are positioned facing each other in dynamic poses, as if frozen in an act of performance or storytelling. Their clothing features elements that flow off their shoulders and arms, decorative buttons down their torsos, and ribbons around their hips. In the background, there are groups of smaller people engaged in various activities, including some who appear to be dancing. On the left is a small tree and the faint outline of a building, and in the center there is the small outline of a church tower. The sky above the scene is blank, and below the central people there are the words “Pasquariello Truonno Meo Squaquara.” The print is in dark lines on off-white paper.

artworks.title: Fracischina and Gian Farina
artworks.description: This is an image of two figures engaged in a lively scene, possibly a dance or performance, with an audience in the background. The image shows a female figure on the left with her arms raised high, holding an item that appears to be a tambourine, and a male figure on the right lifting a sword overhead. Both figures are in motion, with their legs bent and positioned as if they are about to take a step or leap. There are smaller groups of figures in the background, some watching, some moving. The backdrop consists of simple architectural structures, suggesting an outdoor setting, possibly a town square or marketplace. The drawing is rendered with fine lines and light shading.

artworks.title: Franca Trippa and Fritellino
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two costumed figures labeled "Franca Trippa" and "Fritellino" engaged in a lively, theatrical scene. The primary subjects of the drawing are two individuals dressed in elaborate, exaggerated costumes, complete with long feathered hats and masks. "Franca Trippa," positioned on the left, appears to be holding a large exaggerated fork, and is animatedly balanced on one foot. "Fritellino," on the right, holds a string instrument in a poised position while in motion, also on one foot. In the background, a village scene is depicted, with small groups of figures engaged in dance or festive activities, set among buildings that suggest a quaint town or village environment. The style is detailed and theatrical, reflecting an atmosphere of performance or merriment.

artworks.title: Taglia Cantoni and Fracasso
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures in a sword fight. The image shows two fancifully dressed figures frozen in a dynamic stance as they cross swords. Both figures wear costumes with wide-brimmed hats adorned with feathers, fitted garments, and capes. The figure on the left is labeled "Taglia Cantoni," with a more assertive forward posture, while the one on the right, "Fracasso," stands with a defensive stance. The background includes smaller figures, possibly an audience. The use of lines and shading emphasizes the dramatic motion and attire, common in caricature or theatrical illustrations.

artworks.title: Cap. Cardoni and Maramao
artworks.dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 8 × 10 cm (3 1/8 × 3 15/16 in.)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures engaged in a confrontation with spears. The scene features one figure labeled as "Cap. Cardoni" and the other as "Maramao." Both are dressed in costume-like outfits. The background includes small groups of additional figures and outlines of buildings, setting the confrontation in an urban environment. The illustration is rendered in a monochromatic style with fine line work and a sense of dynamic motion in the figures' postures.

artworks.title: Cap. Mala Gamba and Cap. Bellavita
artworks.description: The image shows two figures standing in dynamic poses. The figure on the left, labeled "Cap˙ Mala Gamba," is holding a large feathered hat above their head. The figure on the right, labeled "Cap˙ Bellavita," is extending a stick or sword with one hand while holding a hat with plumes. A group of smaller figures is in the background, engaged in an activity. The setting includes sparse trees and distant buildings reminiscent of a town or village.

artworks.title: Cap. Babeo and Cucuba
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two characters in vibrant costumes in a village setting. The figures are engaging in exaggerated poses. One character, labeled 'Cap Babeco,' is standing hunched with a row of buttons on the outfit. The other character, labeled 'Cucuba,' is in a dynamic pose with raised arms. The background features buildings and smaller figures. The style is reminiscent of traditional Italian commedia dell'arte.

artworks.title: Cap. Esgangarato and Cap. Cocodrillo
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two fantastical figures engaged in a dynamic pose with smaller figures in the background. The two central figures have exaggerated features, elongated limbs, and eerie, bird-like masks. They are adorned with various items and are depicted in energetic gestures. Smaller figures in the background seem to mimic them. The background shows a building and trees in an outdoor setting. Captions beneath the figures name them 'Csgangarato' and 'Cocodrillo.' The detailed line work adds expressiveness to the scene.

artworks.title: Smaralo Cornuto and Ratsa di Boio
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring two grotesque anthropomorphic figures in a theatrical setting. The figure on the left has elongated legs, a hunched posture, and carries a grotesque mask with a long, beak-like nose topped with pointed horns. The character on the right has muscular forearms, a bulbous body with embellishments, and a head with extended feather-like decorations. In the background, there are smaller figures and buildings, suggesting a street or plaza setting. The artistic style features expressive linework and a whimsical, motion-filled scene.

artworks.title: Cap. Spessa Monti and Bagattino
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures in costume performing with a crowd in the background. The drawing depicts two characters in exaggerated theatrical costumes. The figure on the left is labeled "Cap. Spessa Monti" and wields a sword with a dramatic stance. The figure on the right is labeled "BaGattino" and strikes a comical pose with an amused expression. A group of smaller figures are shown in the background interacting with each other. The focus is on theatrical tradition, with detailed costumes and expressive body language.

artworks.title: Scapino and Cap. Zerbino
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures engaged in a discussion or negotiation. The scene captures a dynamic interaction between two characters dressed in theatrical costumes, complete with hats adorned with feathers and outfits that include capes and exaggerated facial masks. To the left stands a tall figure with the name "Scapino" beneath it, wearing loose clothing and holding gesturing hands, accompanied by a sword at their waist. To the right stands "Cap. Zerbino," also swaying as they speak, notably clutching a coat that flows over their buttons and standing on similarly styled footwear. In the background, there is a lively scene with buildings, trees, and smaller figures, some of which appear to be in motion or engaged in an activity involving sticks or swords.

artworks.title: Cap. Cerimonia and Siga. Lavinia
artworks.description: The image shows two figures in full body view. On the left is a character labeled "Cap. Cerimonia" standing with a slightly bent posture and head tilted to the right. This figure has exaggerated facial features, a large pointed nose, broad grin, and a wing-like structure emerging from the back. The character wears a long, buttoned garment with an elongated shoe and holds a theatrical mask with streamers. On the right is "Sig. Lauma," a female figure standing upright and slightly turned to the left. She wears a large feathered hat and has an elegant hairstyle with curled hair framing her face. She is dressed in a long gown with her right hand on her hip. Both figures are in an open courtyard or plaza with smaller figures in the background engaged in various festive activities and dancing. Simple buildings with facades and the characters' names inscribed below them can be seen.

artworks.title: Scaramucia and Fricasso
artworks.description: The image depicts two figures engaged in a sword duel. The figure on the left is in a lunging stance with a sword in their right hand, while the figure on the right is also in a lunging pose with a sword in their left hand. Both figures wear hats with feathers and loose-fitting outfits. In the background, there are other people with feathered hats. The text below the image shows the names 'Scaramucia' and 'Fricasso.'

artworks.title: Cucorongna and Pernoualla
artworks.dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 8 × 9.8 cm (3 1/8 × 3 7/8 in.)
artworks.description: The image depicts two anthropomorphic figures positioned side-by-side in a dynamic stance. These figures have a humanoid shape but appear to be bird-like creatures with large beak-like structures, extensive plumage, and thin limbs. Their heads are adorned with multiple feathers. They are not wearing traditional clothing, but their bodies are covered with what resembles feathers or fur. They stand on a plain background with drawn figures resembling spectators and a possible stage or platform indicated by an uneven horizontal line. The setting features faintly depicted architectural structures in the background. The figures are captioned "Cucorongna" and "Pernoualla."

artworks.title: Guatsetto and Mestolino
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two large, anthropomorphic bird-like figures engaged in a confrontation. The drawing features two figures with exaggerated features facing each other, each wearing wide-brimmed hats adorned with long feathers and holding swords. Their attire is reminiscent of 16th or 17th-century European fashion. The scene is lively with numerous smaller figures in the background, some with similar bird-like features, engaged in various activities such as gesturing or cheering. The composition suggests a theatrical or comical scenario, with the names "Guatsofro" and "Mestolino" inscribed beneath each primary figure. The style suggests a satirical or caricatured portrayal, capturing a sense of drama and humor.

artworks.title: Pride (Vanity)
artworks.medium: etching and engraving on laid paper
artworks.dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 8.1 × 6.4 cm (3 3/16 × 2 1/2 in.)
artworks.description: The image is an etching featuring a full-length view of a person in motion. The figure is turned slightly to the left, with one foot raised. They have delicate facial features, with finely drawn eyes and lips, as well as short, curly hair under a large headdress. The person wears a voluminous gown with puffy sleeves, an ornate collar, and holds a mirror in their left hand and a small object in their right hand. A peacock stands near their feet, and a winged creature holds a ribbon connected to the person's clothing. In the background is a plain surface with the word "Superbia" and the artist's signature "I. Callot" visible.

artworks.title: Sloth
artworks.medium: etching and engraving on laid paper
artworks.dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 8.2 × 6.5 cm (3 1/4 × 2 9/16 in.)
artworks.description: The image shows a person sitting on the ground with their head slightly bowed and hands resting on their lap. The person has long hair, a somber expression, and wears a long robe. Behind them is a structure resembling a resting beast with ornate horns. Above them is a small winged creature with bat-like wings. The background is plain with a textured appearance. The word "Pigrizia" is written below the person in bold lettering.

artworks.title: Lust
artworks.medium: etching and engraving on laid paper
artworks.dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 8.1 × 6.3 cm (3 3/16 × 2 1/2 in.)

artworks.title: Anger
artworks.medium: etching and engraving on laid paper
artworks.dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 8.2 × 6.5 cm (3 1/4 × 2 9/16 in.)
artworks.description: The image shows a figure standing in a dynamic pose. The person is leaning slightly forward with their right arm extended upward, holding a sword. Their left arm is raised to the side, holding a circular shield. The individual's hair appears to be mid-length and is flowing. They have a sharp facial expression, with prominent features. The figure is dressed in a tunic or armor with detailed textures indicating fabric folds. A lion is positioned behind the figure, and a small winged creature is above them. The background is simple, with minimal details. The word "Ira" is written at the bottom. The entire illustration is created in a sketch or engraving style.

artworks.title: Gluttony
artworks.medium: etching and engraving on laid paper
artworks.dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 8 × 6.3 cm (3 1/8 × 2 1/2 in.)
artworks.description: This is an image of an allegorical figure. The drawing shows a female figure in traditional attire holding a goblet and a basket. Above her head is a bat-like creature perched upon her. A pig is reclining at her feet. The word "Gula" is inscribed beneath the woman. The drawing represents the sin of gluttony. The artwork displays intricate linework and detail in the classical style.

artworks.title: Envy
artworks.medium: etching and engraving on laid paper
artworks.dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 8.2 × 6.5 cm (3 1/4 × 2 9/16 in.)
artworks.description: This is an image of a scene featuring a figure with elongated limbs and flowing garments, accompanied by a small dog-like creature and a winged demon perched on its head. The image includes the text "Invidia" at the bottom. The figure appears to be in motion, with hair and clothing billowing backwards. The figure holds a serpent in one hand and the other hand clutches its own chin. The dog-like creature beside them seems to snarl or bark. The winged demon on the figure's head adds an additional layer to the drawing. The style is reminiscent of works from the Renaissance.

artworks.title: Greed
artworks.medium: etching and engraving on laid paper
artworks.dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 8 × 6.2 cm (3 1/8 × 2 7/16 in.)
artworks.description: This is an image of a figure against a plain background. The central figure is labeled "Avaritia" at the bottom. The figure is dressed in a flowing garment and holding a bag. The head of the figure is adorned with branches or antler-like appendages. Surrounding the figure are objects resembling bags or containers. The drawing features fine lines and a minimalist style emphasizing themes of greed and excess.
